result.title: A Simple Doxastic Deontic Logic for Norm-Guided Decision Making
result.comment: Manuscript accepted at PRIMA 2026. Includes an additional appendix with proofs
result.summary: Making decisions despite conflicting norms and incomplete or unreliable information is a fundamental challenge for autonomous systems. We introduce a simple doxastic deontic logic for this setting: a classically reducible fragment of Chellas' Minimal Deontic Logic, extended with explicit conditional norms and combined with multi-agent KD45, so that norms can depend on agents' beliefs about both facts and norms. On this logic we define the Doxastic Norm Compliance Optimization Problem, where an agent chooses a decision minimizing weighted norm violations. We distinguish subjective optimization (relative to the agent's beliefs) from objective optimization (relative to the actual facts). We give conditions under which (i) the two coincide and (ii) optimal decision-making can be reduced to weighted partial MaxSAT in polynomial time.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出一种简化的信念道义逻辑，将 Chellas 极小道义逻辑的可归约片段与带显式条件规范的信念逻辑及多智能体 KD45 结合，使规范依赖智能体对事实与规范的信念，并据此定义「信念规范合规最优化问题」，区分相对信念的主观最优化与相对事实的客观最优化，给出二者一致的条件及归约为加权部分 MaxSAT 的多项式时间结论。
AI.relevance_reason: 其主观/客观优化的区分与信念下规范依赖，可能为 LVR 中「答案是否真正使用内部 latent 内容」的视觉旁路诊断、以及信念状态与证据筛选的决策建模提供形式化线索，可供核查而非直接迁移。
